previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, alcohol dependence, and chronic pain from prior trauma, was admitted after returning to the emergency department with severe shortness of breath and alcohol intoxication. He had left AMA the prior day but returned due to worsening respiratory symptoms. Imaging showed recurrent right middle lobe collapse and findings consistent with acute on chronic aspiration, but no malignancy. He was treated for a COPD exacerbation with oral steroids and antibiotics, and for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam and supportive vitamins. His sodium normalized with oral hydration, and he was weaned off oxygen. Despite clinical improvement, he elected to leave against medical advice on hospital day two, declining discharge medications and follow-up instructions due to dissatisfaction with pain management. He was warned of the risks of untreated withdrawal and respiratory decline.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, unspecified

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ year-old man with history of COPD and EtOH 
abuse presenting with dyspnea and alcohol intoxication which is 
likely a COPD exacerbation.  

Active Issues:

# Shortness of breath: Given patient's significant hx of COPD, 
and lack of any clear infiltrate on xray, no leukocytosis with 
no left shift and no fevers since patient has arrived, this is 
likely secondary to COPD flare or aspiration pneumonitis (given 
significant ETOH intake), as patient is hypoxic, dyspneic and 
with sputum production. COPD exacerbation likely triggered by 
some aspiration pneumonitis and atelectasis. EKG has no ischemic 
changes that would be suspicious for cardiac cause and no 
tachycardia and low pre-test probability for PE. Pt was given 
albuterol and ipratropium nebs, prednisone 40mg, and 
azithromycin. He improved clinically with less shortness of 
breath and reduction in his cough. 
 
# ETOH abuse: Patient had serum EtOH level ~260 on admission. Pt 
now experiencing withdrawal symptoms. Scoring on CIWA and 
requiring benzos. Patient has previously reported history of 
withdrawal seizures and DT. He was monitored on a CIWA scale 
with Valium. He was given folate, thiamine, and MVI.  He 
continued to score on CIWA and signed out AMA.

# Hypertension: BP was elevated. This was likely from a 
combination of alcohol withdrawal and primary hypertension. Pt 
was continued on enalapril, metoprolol, and HCTZ. Pt will need 
his BP re-evaluated when he is not going through withdrawal to 
determine if he needs changes to his anti-hypertensive regimen.  

 
# Tobacco abuse: Pt with a long history of tobacco abuse (1 PPD 
smoker x ___ years). Pt was encouraged to quit given his 
significant lung disease and current COPD exacerbation. He was 
started on nicotine patch and gum. He was counseled on benefits 
of smoking cessation.
